analysis: Examined base_text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md lines 386-1226. The only changed region in the supplied range map is the `darkbloom update` flag table (base 743-745; head 743-747, 751-769) plus head 1852/1859-1860, which are outside the supplied units. The patch excerpt documents a new `update --rollback` mode: it restores the retained predecessor, quarantines the installed release, contacts no coordinator, requires `--yes` without a TTY, drains via the watchdog's journaled rollback under the update lease, and rearms the watchdog (UpdateRollback.swift). This is documentation only; no source implementation was supplied. Security relevance: T-043 (watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable provider binary) and T-013/T-034/T-054 (an operator-triggered downgrade to an older signed build). A downgrade is an operator action on their own Mac (ADV-001 already controls the binary per TB-003), and serving authorization remains coordinator-evaluated against qualification/revocation generations (TB-011, T-054). That means local rollback should not by itself grant serving permission to a revoked build. However, this contract is unverified here. Integration should confirm in UpdateRollback.swift and SelfUpdater.swift that rollback cannot restore a build the coordinator has revoked or disqualified into serving, and that the quarantine/`--override-quarantine` interplay cannot be abused. It should also confirm that the update lease and single-instance lock prevent races with logout and recovery (A-008 logout lease semantics), and check whether T-043 and the threat model need an update for the user-invoked rollback path. No concrete regression is visible in the supplied doc text, and the remaining base text is unchanged.
